name: Sarah Pratt McLean Greene
bio: Sarah Pratt McLean Greene (1856–1935) was an American writer, born at Simsbury, Connecticut, and educated at Mount Holyoke College. She is known for books of Cape Cod life such as Cape Cod Folks and Vesty of the Basins.
Rittenhouse included her dialect poem “De Massa ob de Sheepfol’”, which she judged destined to hold a lasting place.

poems.title: De Massa ob de Sheepfol'
poems.author: Sarah Pratt McLean Greene
poems.collection: The Little Book of Modern Verse (1913)
poems.text:
De massa ob de sheepfol'
 Dat guard de sheepfol' bin,
Look out in de gloomerin' meadows
 Whar de long night rain begin --
So he call to de hirelin' shephe'd:
 "Is my sheep -- is dey all come in?"

Oh den, says de hirelin' shephe'd,
 "Dey's some, dey's black and thin,
And some, dey's po' ol' wedda's --
 But de res', dey's all brung in.
 But de res', dey's all brung in."

Den de massa ob de sheepfol'
 Dat guard de sheepfol' bin,
Goes down in de gloomerin' meadows
 Whar de long night rain begin --
So he le' down de ba's ob de sheepfol',
 Callin' sof':  "Come in!  Come in!"
 Callin' sof':  "Come in!  Come in!"

Den up t'ro de gloomerin' meadows,
 T'ro de col' night rain an' win',
An' up t'ro de gloomerin' rain-paf
 Whar de sleet fa' piercin' thin --
De po' los' sheep ob de sheepfol'
 Dey all comes gadderin' in.
De po' los' sheep ob de sheepfol',
 Dey all comes gadderin' in!
